doc.title: Terry Gibbs interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, November 5, 2021 [interview 2 of 2]

title: Jack Sheldon, Chubby Jackson and Joe Maini
summary: Gibbs describes working with Jack Sheldon at Disneyland, keeping him clean, and notes Joe Maini and Chubby Jackson as characters.

story.theme_name: Working for Benny Goodman: the leader and his bands
story.community_name: Working for Benny Goodman: the perfectionist bandleader

blocks.x: Um hum. If I put Terry Gibbs and Jack Sheldon and Chubby Jackson in a room together, I wonder what might occur?

Well first you’d have to call the insane asylum. You call the insane asylum and make a reservation at the insane asylum. Because I don’t know it would be a lot of laughs. Talk about — Chubby and I had — a completely differently than Jack and I did. I’ll tell you about Jack. You know Jack could get a little risqué on stage. But when he worked with me he knew that he could not do that. I’m selling music and I’ll be the straight man, and Jack is funny without having to be dirty. You know he’s funny. He’s got a great mind. So we had a thing going. We played at the Carnation Hall over at Disneyland. And I hired Jack, because Jack had a good following. And I always featured Jack at the end of the set before I played my ballad, the closing tune, I’d feature Jack. And when I’d announce his name half the audience would come running over to the stage, you know, at Carnation Hall, because they wanted to see Jack because he was funny. And they expected to hear all these — hey but this was Disneyland, you know, Mom and Pop. And he’d say, “Oooh it’s so great to be here at Disneyland” and they he would say, “it’s nice to be here with Minnie, Mickey and Minnie Mouse” and the moment he’d say Minnie Mouse I’d go right into the music. We made that up because people expected him for many miles to go into one of his routines about some off-the-wall out there with a female, you know. That was Jack Sheldon. Joe Maini was the guy you never had to [inaudible] to. You learned what I wrote about him, about Joe Maini, what he said when it was his birthday with the Dream Band played “Happy Birthday” to him, you heard about the Dream Band. You’d never hand him a mic because he — he was street people.
